title: E-Commerce BlinkIt vs Zepto vs JioMart Reviews Analysis
research_question_or_purpose: Compare customer satisfaction and recurring complaint topics across Blinkit, Zepto, and JioMart
data_source: Scraped Google Play reviews (4,620 rows across Blinkit, Zepto, JioMart)
method: NLP tokenization, VADER sentiment scoring, keyword complaint matching, word clouds, Matplotlib bar charts
principal_contribution: Demonstrates basic cross-platform sentiment scoring and keyword complaint proportions
overlap_with_our_project: Overlaps in basic sentiment scoring and complaint topic extraction; lacks CRM framework, economic prioritization, or switching intention analysis
limitation: No CRM service-recovery framework; no switching intention tracking; no economic cost-benefit trade-off; JioMart instead of Instamart

title: Quick Commerce Review Insights: Blinkit vs Zepto vs JioMart
research_question_or_purpose: Evaluate quick commerce sentiment trends and complaint proportions over time
data_source: 4,620 rows (identical to mdaniq45 with reformatted dates)
method: Python, Pandas, Seaborn monthly sentiment aggregation, complaint percentage calculation
principal_contribution: Reports platform-level complaint percentages (e.g., Blinkit delivery 43%, Zepto support 21%, JioMart cancellations 27%)
overlap_with_our_project: Overlaps on complaint percentage reporting by platform; does not bridge findings to CRM interventions
limitation: Derivative dataset; zero independent observations; purely descriptive post-hoc reporting without decision framework

title: Blinkit Review Discovery Engine
research_question_or_purpose: Understand why Blinkit users stay locked inside 2-3 categories and diagnose customer friction
data_source: Multi-source ingestion: 32k Play Store reviews, 3.2k YouTube comments, App Store, Nykaa/Amazon PDP proxies
method: Embeddings, LanceDB vector search, Gemini LLM enrichment, validation scorecard (gold-set classifier accuracy, inter-run stability 83.3%, citation audit)
principal_contribution: Sophisticated multi-source review discovery and RAG conversational search over Blinkit customer feedback
overlap_with_our_project: Overlaps on Blinkit customer friction discovery and category expansion barriers; technically sophisticated pipeline with validation procedures
limitation: Single-platform focus (Blinkit only); YouTube data lacks ratings; focuses on catalog expansion rather than competitor service-recovery economics; unlicenced

title: The Rise of Quick Commerce: Analyzing Consumer Preferences and Buying Behavior in India
author_or_owner: Dr. Guruprasad R. Naik & Girish Kapdi
research_question_or_purpose: Identify primary adoption drivers and demographic relationships in Indian quick commerce
data_source: Secondary data synthesis of published industry reports (NIQ 2024, Deloitte 2023, PwC 2023, KPMG 2023)
method: Descriptive statistical aggregation, crosstabs, Chi-Square hypothesis testing
principal_contribution: Confirms convenience (78%) and speed (65%) dominate discounts (57%) as adoption drivers; notes youth/urban skew
overlap_with_our_project: Contextual validation that speed/convenience drive loyalty while discounts drive trial; justifies focus beyond discounts
limitation: Pure secondary synthesis; zero empirical review or customer-level dataset; provides macro findings but no operational CRM decision guidance

title: Quick Commerce and Customer Retention: A Study of Blinkit and Zepto
research_question_or_purpose: Evaluate whether ultra-fast delivery and discounting sustain long-term customer retention
data_source: Survey of urban consumers using Blinkit and Zepto in India
method: Quantitative regression and descriptive factor analysis
principal_contribution: Establishes that speed and discounts drive trial, but service reliability and support responsiveness dictate retention
overlap_with_our_project: Direct conceptual alignment with our core thesis (service recovery protects retention better than blanket discounts)
limitation: Academic survey methodology; does not provide an actionable CRM decision matrix or public-feedback prioritisation framework

title: Customer Loyalty in India's Quick Commerce Industry: A Case Study of Swiggy Instamart
research_question_or_purpose: Analyze CLV and repeat usage predictors as customer acquisition costs rise in Indian quick commerce
data_source: Urban consumer survey data on Swiggy Instamart usage
method: Multivariate statistical analysis, regression of service quality factors on repeat usage
principal_contribution: Identifies delivery accuracy and operational reliability as primary predictors of repeat purchase; maps failure points
overlap_with_our_project: Aligns with our focus on service failure points triggering platform defection
limitation: Firm-specific academic case study; relies on primary survey rather than public customer reviews; lacks economic recovery simulation

title: Instant Gratification: Understanding Customer Loyalty in Quick Commerce Mobile Apps Using SEM-ANN-NCA
research_question_or_purpose: Determine threshold levels of service quality and convenience required to curb switching risk
data_source: Cross-sectional survey of 330 quick-commerce app users
method: Hybrid Partial Least Squares SEM, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA)
principal_contribution: Demonstrates that service quality is a necessary condition for app stickiness and satisfaction
overlap_with_our_project: Supports the causal chain that operational service quality mitigates switching risk in quick commerce
limitation: Focuses on complex predictive modeling (SEM-ANN) rather than practical CRM prioritisation rules; no operational decision framework
